audit.why: 48.86% over 837 games — a genuine losing lane. Jayce owns levels 1-2 on cannon range, it evens at 3, and Sett takes 4-5 through first item on grit and Haymaker before it settles near even late.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart reads Skill|Skill|Skill|Jayce|Skill|Jayce|Jayce, which contradicts the page's own text at every stage: whys[0]/[1] say you out-range him, whys[2] says 'It evens out', whys[3]/[4]/[5] all describe Sett winning, and late says it 'settles back to even'.
audit.why: Both the prose and the packet reference chart read Jayce|Jayce|Skill|Sett|Sett|Sett|Skill. A chart that hands Jayce the first-item stage while the caption underneath says his first bruiser item reclaims the lane is actively misleading.
audit.corrected: win[] and phases[].side set to Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Sett, Sett, Sett, Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (a) Facebreaker is called a 'grab-stun' throughout — Riot: it pulls in enemies on OPPOSITE sides of Sett, and 'if enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned'. (b) The Show Stopper's grounding is never mentioned. (c) Haymaker's centre is TRUE damage and the page never says so. Ability name written as 'Show Stopper'; it is 'The Show Stopper'.
audit.why: (a) changes how you stand: alone against Sett with no minion behind you, his E is a slow, not a lock. (b) is decisive — grounding shuts off To the Skies!, Jayce's only dash, so the R takes away the escape the page tells you to use. (c) makes armour the wrong buy against his biggest hit.
audit.corrected: All three stated, and the ult named The Show Stopper.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flagged defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere.
audit.why: Haymaker is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, The Show Stopper 120/100/80s, Knuckle Down 9s. Haymaker's 18s at rank 1 is the window to commit in.
audit.corrected: mid now says bait the 18s Haymaker then commit inside its cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warns that flat armour is a poor answer.
audit.why: Haymaker's centre is true damage; stacking armour reads the trade wrong. Health and disengage beat resistances here.

edits.before: This is where it tilts to Sett. Through Levels 4-5 his base stats and a charged Haymaker out-trade your melee Hammer combo, and at 6 his Show Stopper suppress-slam into Haymaker is a real all-in your kit lacks — your stance-swap is mobility, not a burst spike. Never get Facebreaker-grabbed near his tower in this window; your only escape from a landed R is the Hextech Capacitor move speed off a swap. Keep poking from gate-Q range, bait his Haymaker (grit decays if he can't connect), and refuse the extended brawl he wants.
edits.after: This is where it tilts to Sett. Through Levels 4-5 his base stats and a charged Haymaker out-trade your melee Hammer combo, and at 6 The Show Stopper grounds you mid-slam — grounding shuts off To the Skies!, so the Hextech Capacitor swap speed is your only out. Facebreaker stuns only when it catches you on the opposite side from another target; alone you are merely slowed, so never stand off his flank. Bait the 18s Haymaker and refuse the brawl, then run your whole pattern inside its cooldown.

edits.before: It settles back to even. You both drop off as hard carries, but Sett's Show Stopper engage and grit give him more teamfight relevance than your fading poke-burst, while your squishy frame gets deleted if his E grab into Haymaker into R ever connects in a skirmish. Your job is to have already spent the early edge: take plates and prio in Levels 1-2, then sidelane and poke objectives from max gate-Q range. Don't gamble a two-item all-in into a charged Haymaker — chip him and let your team punish his committed R.
edits.after: It settles back to even. You both drop off as hard carries, but Sett's R, The Show Stopper, and his grit give him more teamfight relevance than your fading poke-burst, while your squishy frame gets deleted if his E into Haymaker into R ever connects in a skirmish. Your job is to have already spent the early edge: take plates and prio in Levels 1-2, then sidelane and poke objectives from max gate-Q range. Never all-in a charged Haymaker — its centre is true damage, so armour will not save you.

edits.before: His Show Stopper suppress-slam into Haymaker is a true all-in and your swap is no burst spike — never be E-grabbed near his tower here.
edits.after: The Show Stopper grounds you mid-slam, killing To the Skies! as an escape, and your swap is no burst spike — never brawl near his tower here.

edits.before: Land a Facebreaker E grab-stun to lock you for the Haymaker plus heavy Pit Grit punch — his whole all-in hinges on it
edits.after: Catch you on his far side so Facebreaker (E) stuns instead of slows, then unload Haymaker plus a Pit Grit right punch

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are yours: take Cannon Q and gate-Q (fire Shock Blast through Acceleration Gate) every time Sett walks up to last-hit, and the swap shred (Armor/MR on the first hit after stance-swap) lets you chunk him before he has grit banked for Haymaker. The whole danger is his Facebreaker E grab — if he lands it he gets a free charged Haymaker plus a heavy Pit Grit punch, so respect grab range and poke from max range. Do not sit in melee trading autos; his grit-trade beats yours, so keep it a ranged orb war while you hold the range edge.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours: take Cannon Q and gate-Q (fire Shock Blast through Acceleration Gate) every time Sett walks up to last-hit, and the swap shred (Armor/MR on the first hit after stance-swap) lets you chunk him before he has grit banked for Haymaker. The whole danger is his Facebreaker E — land it with a target on your far side and he gets a stun into a charged Haymaker, so respect the 16s E and poke from max range. Never trade autos in melee: Haymaker's centre is true damage, so armour is the wrong buy here.

notes: Facebreaker only stuns when it pulls enemies from opposite sides of Sett — isolated it is a slow. The page called it a grab-stun unconditionally. The Show Stopper's grounding (it shuts off To the Skies!) and Haymaker's true-damage centre were both absent and are the two facts that decide this lane.
